name: Ultra Pink
lede: Ultra Pink is a hot, electric pink-magenta, most closely tied to the fluorescent crayons of the 1970s and the colors of punk.

sections.title: A fluorescent crayon
sections.body:
By St Clair's account, Crayola's limited fluorescent set of 1972 had eight crayons, among them ultra pink and hot magenta, and every one glowed under black light [1]. Fluorescents were the novelty of the decade, louder versions of the bright colors of 1960s advertising and pop art [1]. Punk adopted the loudest pinks for dyed hair and album lettering [1].

The screen swatch cannot glow. It is the color's closest ordinary screen value, taken from a reference list, and the glow of the crayon came from fluorescence, which a screen does not copy [2]. In the ISCC-NBS system this swatch is nearest to "brilliant purple", 10.6 CIEDE2000 units away, a loose fit [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Ultra Pink hardly exists in museum painting [3]. No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1 per cent of its canvas, within a CIEDE2000 distance of 4, as photographed [3]. That describes the archive, not painting as a whole; its colors were made for fluorescent crayons and punk posters, not oil on panel [1][3].

origin.source: St Clair, The Secret Lives of Color
